en.title: Miami Sheriff Unfazed by GTA 6 'Vice City' Takeover Despite Criminality Concerns
en.summary: Despite initial strong opposition from local law enforcement regarding the glorification of crime, promotional efforts for Grand Theft Auto 6's Vice City setting are moving forward in Miami. A prominent NBA arena has embraced the fictional city's branding, showcasing a stark contrast to the sheriff's earlier stance.
en.body:
The vibrant, crime-ridden streets of **Vice City** are set to make a grand return with **Grand Theft Auto 6**, and while **Rockstar Games** and **Take-Two Interactive** are leaning heavily into the game's real-world inspiration in Florida, not everyone is thrilled. **Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz** previously voiced strong disapproval of promotional activities that would associate the county with the franchise's notorious criminal underworld. At the time, she characterized **Grand Theft Auto** as "a videogame franchise built around criminal activity," citing its fictional depiction of murder, robbery, drug trafficking, and violence against law enforcement as antithetical to the daily efforts of her office.

Despite these concerns, the promotional push for **GTA 6** has largely continued, demonstrating a willingness from some entities to embrace the game's cultural impact. The City of Miami Beach approved a "discreet" campaign, but it's the Kaseya Center, home to the NBA's Miami Heat, that has made the most striking statement. The arena prominently displayed a "Welcome to Vice City" sign visible to air travelers, a bold move that directly engages with the game's aesthetic. This visibility was amplified in October with the "Night in Vice City" campaign, which saw the arena and the Heat team undergo a full rebranding in **Vice City** livery, turning a significant local landmark into a temporary homage to the game.

## Embracing the Vice

This evolution from official concern to public spectacle underscores a common tension in the entertainment industry. While law enforcement officials like Sheriff Cordero-Stutz and Commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez have highlighted the potential for such promotions to inadvertently glorify criminal activity, the allure of a major cultural phenomenon like **Grand Theft Auto** proved too strong for some. The NBA's involvement, particularly with a high-profile team like the Miami Heat, signals a significant mainstream acceptance of the **Vice City** brand. It’s a testament to how deeply video games have permeated popular culture, with even those initially resistant finding ways to capitalize on or participate in the hype surrounding one of the most anticipated game releases in years.

## What's Next

As **Grand Theft Auto 6** inches closer to its console release, further promotional activities and potential collaborations are expected. While the initial opposition from **Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office** highlights ongoing debates about the intersection of crime-themed entertainment and public spaces, the current momentum suggests that the fictional **Vice City** will continue to cast a long shadow over its real-world inspiration. Fans eagerly await more details on potential in-game events and future marketing strategies from **Rockstar Games**.

Vice City and Leonida, the fictional city and state that serve as the setting for Grand Theft Auto 6 , are largely based on Miami and the state of Florida, and Rockstar and publisher Take-Two Interactive are moving heavy and hard to leverage that real-life inspiration to promote GTA 6 as its console release gets closer. The sheriff made no bones about her position on the matter when the proposed partnership came to light in September, however, characterizing the game as exactly the sort of thing Miami-Dade shouldn't associate with. "Grand Theft Auto is a videogame franchise built around criminal activity," Cordero-Stutz said at the time. "Its fictional world includes murder, robbery, drug trafficking, carjacking, violence against law enforcement, and other conduct that the men and women of the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office work every single day to prevent." It was a hard line in the sand, but it didn't add up to much. Despite some opposition from local positions, much of it predicated on similar law-and-order concerns, those PR campaigns have moved ahead. The City of Miami Beach voted in September to approve a 'discreet' campaign , for instance, while the Kaseya Center, a downtown arena in Miami that serves as home of the NBA's Miami Heat, took a rather less subtle approach, erecting a massive " Welcome to Vice City " sign on its roof that can be seen by travellers flying into Miami International Airport. The Kaseya Center campaign became even more prominent in October when the Heat, one of the NBA's highest-profile teams, became directly involved via the Night in Vice City campaign, a one-night-only promotion that will see both the arena and the team rebranded in Vice City livery. It is, as former US President Joe Biden once said , "a big fuckin' deal."
